```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
library(AKsf)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
```

Reviewed **2026-09-21**, starting from [NOAA's Alaska fisheries portal](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/region/alaska/fisheries).
This vignette connects NOAA closure resources to AKsf maps. It includes an
offline historical example, a service-discovery recipe, and GMT export.
It does **not** provide a live open/closed decision for a vessel or fishery.

## Find the right kind of restriction

| Resource | What it helps you find | How to use it with AKsf |
|---|---|---|
| [Habitat conservation area maps](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/resource/tool-app/habitat-conservation-area-maps) | Habitat restrictions, including gear-specific protection; PDF and GIS/mobile mapping resources | Overlay the relevant habitat layer on reporting or FMP areas. |
| [Steller sea lion protection measures](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/commercial-fishing/steller-sea-lion-protection-measures) | Prey-fishery protections and links for Atka mackerel, Pacific cod trawl/non-trawl, pollock, and no-groundfish sites | Select the fishery and gear before selecting geometry. |
| [Inseason fisheries management](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/sustainable-fisheries/inseason-fisheries-management-alaska) | Information bulletins, openings/closures, harvest specifications, and status reports | Treat temporal status as a separate source from the spatial boundary. |
| [Status of fisheries](https://alaskafisheries.noaa.gov/status-of-fisheries/) | Groundfish status reports | Record the report date and applicable area, species, and sector. |
| [Figures, maps, boundaries, areas, and zones](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/sustainable-fisheries/alaska-fisheries-figures-maps-boundaries-regulatory-areas-and-zones) | Cross-references to spatial products and regulatory figures | Identify the map and its underlying authority; do not equate every polygon with a closure. |
| [Federal regulations and notices](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/rules-and-regulations/regulations-acts-treaties-and-agreements-federal-fisheries-alaska) | The regulatory framework, including 50 CFR 679 and 680 | Resolve the applicable rule, exceptions, and effective dates against the original material. |

An FMP boundary describes management geography; it is not inherently a fishing
closure. Likewise, essential fish habitat or critical habitat geometry alone
does not encode a universal prohibition. A usable restriction record needs
**place, activity/gear, species or fishery, sector where applicable, time, and
exceptions**. Geometry is only one of those fields.

NOAA's mapping index directs readers to regulations for official closure
information. For current fishing decisions, follow those regulatory and inseason
sources, not the teaching map below.

## Inspect NOAA's spatial service

The [Alaska Regional Office Base_Map service](https://alaskafisheries.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Base_Map/MapServer)
exposes these polygon layers at the time of review:

| Layer ID | Service name | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `NMFS_Reporting_Areas` | Reporting geography, already substantially covered by AKsf. |
| 1 | `Atka_Mackerel` | Fishery-specific integrated spatial restrictions. |
| 2 | `PCod_Trawl` | Pacific cod trawl restriction geography. |
| 3 | `Pcod_Non_Trawl` | Pacific cod non-trawl restriction geography. |
| 4 | `Pollock` | Pollock restriction geography. |
| 5 | `Habitat_Restrictions` | Habitat/restriction composite used for the example below. |
| 6 | `SSL_CH` | Steller sea lion critical habitat context. |
| 7 | `SSL_Zones` | Steller sea lion zones; inspect attributes and linked rules before interpretation. |

Layer IDs belong to this service, not to a universal NOAA catalog. Inspect the
service before reusing an ID. Fields are not standardized across the layers:
for example, layer 4 uses lowercase `htm`, while layer 5 uses `HTM`.
`OBJECTID` is a service feature identifier, not a durable regulatory area code.

The [Spatial Management Areas metadata](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/27352)
describes an integrated product where overlapping restrictions were processed
in a hierarchy. Consequently, a composite feature need not reproduce the full
original footprint of every contributing measure. Do not combine the fishery
composites and habitat layer and count their areas as independent restrictions.
For totals across overlapping polygons, first define the applicable rule set,
then decide whether a union or separate rule-specific totals answer the question.

### Check vintage before mapping

The selected records in [Habitat_Restrictions](https://alaskafisheries.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Base_Map/MapServer/5)
have `dtd = "steve.lewis, akro, 01/19/15"`. The layer metadata did not expose an
`editingInfo` timestamp when inspected. A website update date, retrieval date,
or new download does not establish a new legal effective date. Here `dtd` is
retained as a source annotation, not interpreted as a legal validity interval.

The sample contains just two source records: `GOA_Slope_HCA.htm` and
`GOA_Coral_HPA.htm`. Those records can contain multiple polygon components.
They are a **historical teaching example**, not a comprehensive closure inventory
or certification of the current GOA restrictions.

## Load the pinned example without a network connection

```{r load-example}
example_dir <- system.file("extdata", "closure-example", package = "AKsf")
closures <- st_read(file.path(example_dir, "goa-habitat.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
manifest <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(example_dir, "manifest.json"))
stopifnot(nrow(closures) == manifest$feature_count,
          setequal(closures$OBJECTID, manifest$object_ids),
          !any(st_is_empty(closures)))
knitr::kable(st_drop_geometry(closures)[, c("OBJECTID", "HTM", "dtd")])
```

The accompanying manifest records the service/query URL, object IDs, retrieval
time, SHA-256 checksum, and source annotation. Raw geometry and attributes are
retained as supplied by NOAA, with the service asked to return EPSG:4326.
The example is separate from AKsf's main data catalog and FMP reference layers.

## Map closures as a separate layer

Transform before spatial operations. Keep the source object for traceability;
any validity repair below applies to the mapping copy.

```{r closure-map, fig.cap="Historical NOAA GIS example: selected GOA habitat records, source annotation 2015; retrieved 2026-09-21. This is not a current closure-status map."}
closure_map <- st_transform(closures, proj_aksf())
if (!all(st_is_valid(closure_map))) closure_map <- st_make_valid(closure_map)
labels <- c(GOA_Slope_HCA.htm = "GOA slope habitat conservation",
            GOA_Coral_HPA.htm = "GOA coral habitat protection")
closure_map$map_label <- unname(labels[closure_map$HTM])
bb <- st_bbox(closure_map)
pad <- 100000 # metres in EPSG:3338

ggplot() +
  plot_fmp_areas("GOA_GF", fill = "#e8f1f5", colour = "#7896a5", linewidth = 0.25) +
  plot_reporting_areas(fill = NA, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = closure_map, aes(fill = map_label), colour = "#6e2745", linewidth = 0.5) +
  plot_coast(fill = "grey90", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = c("#d88b54", "#9e77b4")) +
  coord_aksf(xlim = c(bb["xmin"] - pad, bb["xmax"] + pad),
             ylim = c(bb["ymin"] - pad, bb["ymax"] + pad), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_aksf() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 9)) +
  labs(title = "Selected GOA habitat restriction footprints",
       subtitle = "Historical GIS example • source annotation 2015",
       caption = "NOAA AKRO geometry • AKsf FMP reference • Natural Earth land")
```

The pale FMP background supplies context only. The map does not infer that
unshaded water is open or that all fishing is prohibited inside colored areas.
The service's `Shape_Area` values are source attributes; for a spatial analysis,
calculate area from an appropriate equal-area geometry instead of treating Web
Mercator area values as geodesic area.

## Use the same example in GMT

```{r export-gmt}
gmt_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".gmt")
write_gmt(closure_map[, c("OBJECTID", "HTM", "dtd")], gmt_file)
stopifnot(file.exists(gmt_file))
unlink(gmt_file)
```

For a persistent output, replace `gmt_file` with `"goa-habitat-example.gmt"`.
Use `gmt plot goa-habitat-example.gmt` within the map session described in the
[GMT vignette](GMT.html). Preserve the source-vintage label on the GMT figure.
Changing the output format does not change the meaning or currency of the data.

## Discover or refresh source data deliberately

This optional block inspects the service online; it is not executed during
package or website builds:

```{r inspect-service, eval=FALSE}
service <- "https://alaskafisheries.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Base_Map/MapServer"
catalog <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(service, "?f=pjson"))
if (!is.null(catalog$error)) stop(catalog$error$message)
catalog$layers[, c("id", "name")]

metadata <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(service, "/5?f=pjson"))
if (!is.null(metadata$error)) stop(metadata$error$message)
metadata$fields[, c("name", "type")]
metadata$editingInfo # Absence is not evidence of currency.
```

The repository's `data-raw/download-closure-example.py` rebuilds the two-record
snapshot. It first queries matching object IDs, requests those geometries,
checks that every requested ID was returned, and saves metadata and a checksum.
For larger layer downloads, batch the ID list within service limits and verify
completeness; a single successful response can still be truncated. Keep the
original data alongside any transformed, repaired, or simplified derivative.
Review changed geometry and source notes before replacing a published snapshot.

For a time-specific study, record the observation date, species, gear, sector,
source revision, and applicable notices with each analysis. Do not fill absent
season/exception fields by guessing from a layer name or an `HTM` filename.
The `.htm` tokens in this service are retained identifiers, not guaranteed live
URLs or substitutes for the linked regulatory text.

## Relation to the other Alaska packages

Use **akgfmaps** for survey design and strata, **coldpool** for environmental
products, and **AKsf** for FMP/reporting context. A closure polygon is not a survey
stratum. **navmaps** can format operational layers, but this historical example
should not be promoted to a current navigation layer. Maintain the NOAA
restriction source and date independently from each package's basemap version.
